stemMd: Why can evaporation cool the liquid left behind?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Escaping molecules tend to remove more than the average molecular energy.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The liquid’s atoms lose all their protons.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Evaporation always requires the liquid to be at its boiling point.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Evaporation creates cold molecules from nothing.

explanationMd: Molecules energetic enough to escape the surface carry energy away. The remaining liquid can have lower average molecular energy and hence lower temperature unless heat is supplied from outside. This can happen below boiling.

distractorRationale.e: Cooling results from energy distribution and transfer, not creation of a new substance.
distractorRationale.a: They retain thermal motion at the lower temperature.
distractorRationale.c: Evaporation is a phase process, not a nuclear transformation.
distractorRationale.d: Evaporation can occur below the boiling point.
